thread:
Alisha P: quick sync — need to lock Q3 roadmap tradeoffs for console observability. three customer-driven asks: retention cost controls, a lightweight error-analysis UX, and per-service trace-sampling. Acme + FinCorp pressing for trace controls. Thoughts on priority?

Marc R: leaning to prioritize error-analysis MVP first. highest customer-perceived value and smallest surface area.

Yana D: agree on MVP focus, but retention tiering is urgent for finance customers. we should sketch a low-risk tiering approach that doesn't require a full query rewrite.

Tom (SRE): +1 to retention tiering as a cost guardrail. also: any retention change must preserve query latency SLOs for live dashboards.

Sarah PM: proposed lift:
- MVP error-analysis: stack traces, quick-filtering, top-5 errors page (2 sprints)
- Retention tiering: default 7d hot, 30d warm, archive cold (configurable per-org) (3 sprints)
- Trace sampling controls: expose basic sample-rate per-service in console (stretch)
Agree? :eyes:

Marc R: rough infra effort estimates:
```json
{"error_ui":"4 engineer-weeks","retention_tiering":"6 eng-weeks (storage + query flags)","trace_sampling_ui":"3 eng-weeks + api"}
```

Alisha P: good. customers want launch criteria too. propose pass/fail checks:
- error-analysis: must surface actionable triage for >=70% of top-50 incidents in eval set
- retention: config toggles applied without >10% increase in avg query latency (95p)
- trace controls: ability to change sample-rate and see effect in <5m
These can gate GA.

Yana D: I'll own the eval harness for error-analysis. will build a small labeled prompt set + synthetic errors from prod traces. metric: triage precision/recall.

Tom (SRE): I'll run load tests for retention tiers. need to know expected hot->warm promotion rules. sample config idea:
```yaml
retention_tiers:
  hot: 7d
  warm: 30d
  cold: 365d
policies:
  archive_threshold: 90pct_disk_util
```

Marc R: question on UX: error-analysis should let users mark an incident as "investigated" and pin notes. do we need backend mutation? small api yes.

Sarah PM: Yes, add a simple mutation and audit log. keeps scope small.

Alisha P: prioritization vote: comment with A/B/C. A=error-analysis first, retention second, traces stretch. B=retention first, error-analysis second. C=split (parallel teams).

Marc R: A

Yana D: A

Tom (SRE): B (worry about runaway costs)

Sarah PM: A (we can run retention pilot on a few low-risk orgs)

Alisha P: majority A. decision: error-analysis MVP -> retention tier pilot -> trace controls as stretch.

Alisha P: action items:
- Yana: eval harness + labeled set (due 1842600000)
- Marc: API + quick mutation for incident notes (RFC by end of sprint)
- Tom: retention load test plan + pilot checklist (due in 1 week)
- Sarah: customer comms + pilot opt-in list (sync with Acme/FinCorp)

analytics-bot: reminder: roadmap sync tomorrow 10:00am — calendar invite sent.

Alisha P: thanks all — I'll write a short PRD and share for review by EOD.
